newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares add to gains as buyers warm to values.
newsitem.headline: KL shares add to gains as buyers warm to values.

text.p: Kuala Lumpur blue chips built on a 1.6 percent rise on Wednesday to finish up another 1.1 percent as foreign and local buyers warmed up to the market's cheapened values, dealers said.

At the close, the key Composite Index of 100 blue chips ended up 11.82 points or 1.14 percent to 1,045.89, just under its session high of 1,046.69. The Second Board index rose 10.40 points or 1.92 percent to 552.73.
"It would be difficult to turn more negative (on Malaysian stocks)," said an institutional dealer at a local brokerage. He said locals and foreigners were buying.

Easing pressure on interest rates and the ringgit helped restore confidence, dealers said. While the ringgit broke through the key 2.65 a dollar level earlier on Thursday, at 0935 GMT it was quoted at 2.6460/90.
Short-term interest rates have been coming off double-digit levels in the past week.

The stock market's rebound "is confounding quite a few people," said Ami Moris, a vice president in dealing at Capitalcorp. "With the currency turmoil, everybody did not expect the market to head up so strongly and so fast."
Volume was heavy at over 360 million shares, and gainers swamped losers by 612 to 83.
Bakun dam project developer Ekran Bhd ended up five cents to 5.20 ringgit. It said it is still seeking clarification over terms of the dam contract with key contractor ABB Asea Brown Boveri.
Shares of Malaysian Airline ended unchanged at 6.45 ringgit. Its chairman Tajudin Ramli said the company should see no immediate impact from the current ringgit weakness.

On the Kuala Lumpur Options and Financial Futures Exchange, the spot July contract rose 8.8 points to 1,048.8 with 834 contracts traded. August futures gained 7.4 points to 1,048.0, with 305 lots traded.
